title: Arbitrary-size Multi-layer OARSMT RL Router Trained with Combinatorial Monte-Carlo Tree Search
problem: Design multi-layer obstacle-avoiding rectilinear Steiner minimum trees for chip routing by selecting proper Steiner points to minimize wire length while avoiding routing obstacles.
motivation: Efficient routing is fundamental to chip design automation as it directly impacts wire area, power consumption, and overall circuit performance.
method: The router learns to select Steiner points (intermediate routing waypoints) using reinforcement learning, where a neural network gets trained via combinatorial Monte-Carlo tree search—an algorithm that explores placement options by simulating routing outcomes. A 3D U-Net neural network processes the chip layout using a Hanan-grid representation (a standard discretized grid for routing), and can handle layouts of any size and routing configuration in a single forward pass, accounting for varying routing costs across layers.
key_novelty: The core idea is combining combinatorial Monte-Carlo tree search training with a 3D U-Net neural network to select Steiner points for chip routing of any size, all in a single forward pass.
contributions: Novel combinatorial MCTS training approach for RL-based routing
Arbitrary-size routing capability via Hanan-grid representation and 3D U-Net
Single-pass inference for Steiner point selection
Significant performance improvements over algorithmic and RL-based routers

metrics.other: significantly outperforms previous algorithmic routers and Alpha-Go/PPO-based RL routers
